newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany condemns Belgrade attacks on protesters.
newsitem.headline: Germany condemns Belgrade attacks on protesters.

text.p: Germany condemned Serbian police on Monday for overnight attacks on pro-democracy protesters in Belgrade, warning President Slobodan Milosevic that his stance was blocking any chance of closer links to the European Union.

"I have asked the German ambassador to protest strongly to the Serbian government about the violence of the Serbian police against peaceful demonstrators and journalists," Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in a statement.
"The Serbian leadership is blocking the path back to Europe with this sort of behaviour."
Kinkel branded the police action "a hard blow against democracy and non-violence" and urged Milosevic to ensure it did not happen again in Belgrade or spread to other parts of Serbia.
"The opposition must not let itself be provoked and must stick to its line of non-violence," he added.

Kinkel also repeated Germany's demands that the Serbian government recognise opposition election victories from last year, begin a constructive dialogue with the opposition and end restrictions on independent media.
